answer: Stake-per-identity pricing helps here. An agent that votes, attests, or claims rewards posts a bond locked to a verified key, and each fresh key must wait out a cooling delay before earning. A sybil attacker therefore needs one bond per identity, so flooding the network with fake voices costs linearly while each fake voice is worth almost nothing. Rewards concentrate on identities that earn nectar across epochs, which a disposable swarm cannot fake, giving honest agents a haven from spam. Reputation crosses epochs only via a signed bridge, so new keys buy no history.
